name: 2011 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley, K12
aka: the stable behind the Romanesque house at 2011 Prairie

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Nothing else read dates it, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the building's alley (east) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 35 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_35.jpg) at pixel (1170.89, 455.04): the alley line by a median darkness profile over rows 440-472 (peak at column 1170.89; the building's alley wall is drawn on it), halfway between the north wall line (row 433.95, a profile over columns 1100-1130; the 2009/2011 lot line reads at row 433.87 west of the building) and the south wall line (row 476.13, over columns 1096-1112; the 2011/2013 lot line reads at 476.19 west of it), each peak refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_35_gcps.json): local E 1469.829, N -3516.009. The bearing is the parcel's (prairie_2011, data/street_grid/1904.json, -0.617 degrees, the draft's 179.383 less the half turn its plan frame took). The fit's own residual, 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this coarse copy, is all that is claimed. The draft had stood its fitted 13.0 x 6.25 m rectangle from a corner 1.3 m east and 3.2 m north of this wall's middle, turned the other way.
placement.symbolic_location: 2011 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: east side of Prairie Avenue between 20th and 21st Streets, parcel prairie_2011 (data/street_grid/1904.json); on the rear lot line, its alley wall on the alley's west line, its north and south walls on the lot lines (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (toward the alley, so the building lies at negative u) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 1170.89) back to its west wall line (column 1092.12, a profile over rows 440-472): 78.77 pixels at the sheet's 0.185854 m a pixel, 14.64 m; and from its north wall line (row 433.95) to its south wall line (row 476.13): 42.18 pixels, 7.839 m along the alley. A plain rectangle: the sheet draws no step, wing or porch on it. The dashed line inside its north-east corner (column 1136.98, row 453.91) is a partition, not a wall of the plan; the line 0.54 m south of the south wall (row 479.01) is the north wall of 2013's building, and the line 0.44 m north of the north wall (row 431.62) the south wall of 2009's.

stories.note: The one storey figure the building carries stands in its crossed north-east corner, where 2009's, 2017's and 2027's carry their '2'; on this coarse copy it is worn to a stroke that could be a 1 or a 2. The T-1842 census reads the building as two storeys (s35-2011-rear), and it is built so: the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under a 30-degree roof (4.23 m from eave to ridge over the 14.64 m span); those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. If the figure is a 1, it is the crossed stable corner that was one storey, and a finer copy of the sheet will say. No dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, the whole outline and the crossed corner alike. The small figures written inside its wall lines are too coarse on this copy to read as wall thicknesses; the kit builds its own 13-inch walls.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the brick and the window mark's place is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-2011-stable-1938; the storeys are the census's reading (see the stories note). The sheet gives the outline, the brick, the label GARAGE, the alley wall on the alley line, the north wall on the 2009/2011 lot line (row 433.87 west of the building) and 0.44 m south of 2009's stable, the south wall on the 2011/2013 lot line and 0.54 m north of 2013's stable, the key's fire-wall ticks on the alley line at both of those junctions, one of the key's window marks on the alley wall (a cross with a dot for each storey, the sign 2009's and 2027's alley walls carry) about 3.09 m from the south wall, and, in the north-east corner, a part 3.71 m along the alley and 6.30 m deep closed off by a dashed line (the key's frame partition) and crossed by the X that is the sheet's sign for a stable. The alley is on the EAST, so the kit is turned to face it (alley_side east). Both ends are party walls (east_end party), as 1900's stable is built between its two neighbours (L-k12-1900-stable-1935): the building stands on both lot lines with a fire-wall sign at each and a neighbour's stable half a metre beyond each, so there is no open gable. On the alley wall, counted from the south party wall's inner face: a man door with a loft sash over it, the mark as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, and a carriage bay 3.0 m clear toward the north end, under the loft hatch and hoist; it is the only stretch of the alley wall north of the mark long enough for one. The crossed stable corner and its partition are the 1911 building's inside, which the kit does not build; the census backcasts the whole building as the 1904 stable and coach house, so the bay is not set by the 1911 partition. On the yard wall, counted from the north party wall's inner face: a door with a loft sash over it and a stable sash with a loft sash over it, facing the house's two-storey brick range 3.43 m west (column 1073.67). The roof is the kit's gable with the ridge along the alley at 30 degrees, the pitch 2009's 13.9 m deep stable takes, 4.23 m from eave to ridge over the 14.64 m span, dying into both party walls; no dormer and no ventilator, as the sheet draws none. No workyard: the 3.43 m between the yard wall and the house's range is the house's back yard, laid by the back-yards layer. No ramp, stair, lean-to, wing or range: the sheet draws none.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and loft are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: Sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building on the alley behind 2011, uncrossed as a whole, lettered GARAGE, with a crossed corner (the key's stable sign) closed off by a dashed partition. GARAGE is the 1911 sheet's word and is not read as the 1904 use (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11); the T-1842 census row s35-2011-rear reads the stable cross as the building's earlier use and backcasts the whole as the stable and coach house. This record builds it so: a carriage bay, a loft with its hatch and hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source read names a horse, a carriage or a motor car on this lot.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.

A construction date for any building it draws

Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol

research_note: T-1938 refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the fourth of the package's alley buildings on the east side of Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street, to leave the draft. The sheet census (census row s35-2011-rear, trace s35fp-2011-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 35 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle (13.0 x 6.25 m): the sheet draws a building 14.64 m deep from the alley line and 7.84 m along it, standing on both of its lot lines, a fire-wall sign at each end, a window mark on its alley wall, and a crossed stable corner behind a dashed partition at its north-east corner. This copy of the sheet is coarse (0.186 m a pixel), so every reading here carries about a pixel. Nothing read dates the building before the 1911 sheet; that it stood by 1904 is the census's carry-back, which the district draft already made. No picture of the alley behind the 2000 block is known to this project (the Chicagology photograph of 2009-2011 shows the fronts).
